summary: Partial continuation of the 64-item extraction: reclassifies proper H^0 as a pinned-library composite; exposes coherent countable derived limits and Remark 4.3 with the exact shift p^k m; separates algebraic non-Noetherian blowup domination from its integral adic chart adapter; and spells out the comparison-map-only derived splitting argument. The eight inherited source findings remain unchanged and unreviewed. G1–G9 retain precisely scoped residual work; no completeness or formalization claim.

items.name: Regular Noetherian rings
items.statement: IsRegularRing R means R is Noetherian and every prime localization is a regular local ring; the local class uses equality of the finite spanning rank of the maximal ideal and the Krull dimension.

api.name: IsRegularLocalRing.iff_finrank_cotangentSpace
api.statement: Use the existing cotangent-space characterization.

api.name: BhattRegular.localize
api.statement: Request the separate regularity-of-localizations theorem before converting a regular local ring to the global class.

uses.how: Use the existing predicates in the main theorem statements; do not silently identify a local instance with the global predicate without proving localization regularity.

items.name: Faithfully flat module
items.statement: An R-module M is faithfully flat if it is flat and I M is proper for every maximal ideal I of R.

api.name: Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_rTensor_faithful
api.statement: Flatness together with preservation of nonzero modules under tensor is equivalent to faithful flatness.

api.name: Module.FaithfullyFlat.rTensor_reflects_triviality
api.statement: An ordinary faithfully flat tensor product detects the zero module.

uses.how: Ordinary faithful flatness is distinguished from the almost Tor and detection conditions in Proposition 5.2.

items.name: Ordinary adic completion
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I and R-module M, AdicCompletion I M is the module of compatible elements of M/I^n M. IsAdicComplete includes separatedness and convergence of all I-adic Cauchy sequences.

api.name: AdicCompletion.transitionMap
api.statement: Use the existing quotient transition maps.

api.name: BhattCompletion.limit_comparison
api.statement: Identify the completion with the inverse limit of its quotient diagram; do not identify it with a derived limit without hypotheses.

uses.how: Use the existing underived limit; derived completion and preservation of flatness are separate theorems.

items.name: Ordinary derived category
items.statement: For an abelian category C with a chosen HasDerivedCategory instance, DerivedCategory C is the localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms.

api.name: DerivedCategory.Q
api.statement: Use the existing localization functor on cochain complexes.

api.name: BhattDerived.retraction
api.statement: A retraction of the unit is an actual morphism in D(A), with composite the identity.

uses.how: Reuse the triangulated derived category for splitting obstructions; its existence supplies neither derived tensor nor derived inverse limits.

items.name: Artin–Rees
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, submodule N and ideal I, there is k such that for all n≥k, I^n M∩N=I^(n−k)(I^k M∩N).

items.name: Uniform Artin–Rees lifting
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, ideal I and N⊂M, there is k independent of P and the surjection φ:P→N such that every v∈N∩I^(m+k)M lifts through φ to I^m P for every m.

items.name: Krull intersection for a proper ideal
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R, finite R-module M and proper ideal I, the intersection of I^n M is zero; in particular the intersection of I^n in R is zero.

items.name: Chosen compatible roots and their almost ideal
items.statement: Fix a prime p and a nonzerodivisor t in A with specified elements t_n, t_0=t and t_(n+1)^p=t_n. The ideal m_t is generated by all t_n. Almost zero means m_t M=0; the root choices are data.

api.name: RootSystem.root_zero
api.statement: The zeroth root is t.

api.name: RootSystem.root_pow
api.statement: The p-th power of root n+1 is root n.

api.name: RootSystem.almostIdeal_idempotent
api.statement: Prove m_t²=m_t, and verify the flatness/tensor assumptions for almost mathematics.

api.name: RootSystem.map
api.statement: Transport the entire compatible system along a ring map, with identity and composition laws.

uses.how: Use the same chosen root system throughout each transition estimate; the ideals m_t, m_g and m_(tg) are separately named.

items.name: Almost modules and adjoints
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m) with m²=m and the required flatness of m⊗_V m, form the Serre quotient by m-annihilated modules, almostification, its right adjoint (*) and left adjoint (!); for algebras use the distinct (!!) adjoint.
items.note: Field-base supplier: PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base. General reusable-base scope is in the current P0 stage; its stronger adjoint details remain a request.

api.name: Almostification.zero_iff
api.statement: M becomes zero precisely when mM=0.

api.name: AlmostElements.hom
api.statement: Give the right-adjoint Hom equivalence; for a module N, (N^a)_*=Hom_V(m,N).

api.name: AlmostAlgebra.leftAdjoint_reduction
api.statement: Supply (!!) commuting with the reductions used in 5.2, under its actual hypotheses.

uses.how: The module adjoint and algebra adjoint must not be interchanged in the proof of faithful detection.

items.name: Almost flat and almost faithful maps modulo t
items.statement: An algebra map modulo t is almost flat when its positive Tor groups vanish in the specified almost category, and almost faithfully flat when tensor is also conservative there.

api.name: AlmostFlat.tor_vanish
api.statement: Translate almost flatness into almost vanishing of positive Tor.

api.name: AlmostFaithfullyFlat.tensor_reflects_zero
api.statement: Reflect zero in the specified almost category.

api.name: AlmostFaithfullyFlat.comp
api.statement: Compose maps with the same explicitly transported almost base.

uses.how: The 5.2 conclusion detecting ordinary A0-modules is stronger than conservativity only on almost modules and is extracted separately.

items.name: Bhatt's field-based integral perfectoid algebra
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid and t∈K° a topologically nilpotent unit with compatible p-roots and |t|=|p| in characteristic zero. An integral perfectoid K°-algebra is K°-flat, t-adically complete, satisfies A=A_*, and Frobenius A/t^(1/p)→A/t is an isomorphism.

api.name: IntegralPerfectoid.invert
api.statement: A[1/t] is a perfectoid K-algebra with power-bounded ring A.

api.name: IntegralPerfectoid.frobenius_quotient
api.statement: Export the indicated Frobenius isomorphism.

api.name: IntegralPerfectoid.almostElements
api.statement: Replacing an almost integral model by its star produces the stated convention.

uses.how: This is the star-normalized field-based convention of the paper, not every modern general integral perfectoid ring.

items.name: General integral perfectoid ring
items.statement: Use the integral perfectoid notion of PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra, allowing rings which do not contain the valuation ring of a perfectoid field; keep its comparison to Bhatt's field-based convention explicit.

api.name: GeneralPerfectoid.toTate
api.statement: Under the torsion and pseudouniformizer hypotheses used in 5.2, identify the inverted ring as perfectoid.

api.name: GeneralPerfectoid.fieldBaseComparison
api.statement: After adjoining the unit roots and applying star, construct the K°-structure rather than assume it.

uses.how: The ramified construction first produces this broader object. Exact SW-to-BS convention comparison remains G3; this item does not assert an unverified equivalence.

items.name: Perfectoid root disc
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A, let A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩ be the t-adic completion of the compatible-root polynomial algebra and Y=Spa(A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩[1/t],A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩).

api.name: PerfectoidRootDisc.root
api.statement: Export T^(1/p^n) and their power relations.

api.name: PerfectoidRootDisc.lift
api.statement: A bounded compatible-root family gives the continuous evaluation map, uniquely.

api.name: PerfectoidRootDisc.map
api.statement: Base change on coefficients preserves the named roots.

uses.how: The universal root T supplies compatible roots of g after shrinking neighborhoods.

items.name: Integral rational localization with roots
items.statement: For a rational domain in the tilt given by f_i/g, with f_i,g integral and one f_i a power of the tilted pseudouniformizer, its untilted integral ring is almost the completed root-ratio algebra from Scholze Lemma 6.4.

api.name: PerfectoidRational.restrict
api.statement: Nested rational domains give compatible restriction maps.

api.name: PerfectoidRational.rootPresentation
api.statement: Identify the completed root-ratio presentation up to the stated almost isomorphism.

api.name: PerfectoidRational.tilt
api.statement: Tilting identifies this domain with its rational domain in the tilt.

uses.how: Retain the domain and invertibility hypotheses; abstract quotient, torsion-free image and star model are related by almost comparison, not equality.

items.name: Tilt approximation preserving a rational neighborhood
items.statement: For perfectoid affinoid R, f∈R, c≥0 and ε>0, there is h in the tilt with |f(x)−h♯(x)|≤|ϖ|^(1−ε) max(|f(x)|,|ϖ|^c) for all x. For ε<1 the two maxima agree.
items.note: Supplier: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma. Source Corollary 6.7 and packet proof read; the entire Lemma 6.5 proof was not independently reread.

items.name: Shrinking neighborhood algebra B_l
items.statement: For l>0, B_l is O^+ on {|T−g|≤|t|^l} in the perfectoid root disc. Restrictions B_l→B_(l+1) are the direct-system maps.

api.name: RootNeighborhood.restrict
api.statement: Restrictions compose and preserve the root coordinate.

api.name: RootNeighborhood.divisibility
api.statement: T−g is divisible by t^l in B_l.

uses.how: Use the actual restriction maps to pass from local almost flatness to adjoining roots.

items.name: Completed neighborhood extension
items.statement: Set A∞ to the t-adic completion of colim_l B_l; use its star-normalization when necessary. Then T=g in A∞, giving a specified compatible p-root system of g.

api.name: RootExtension.map
api.statement: Construct A→A∞.

api.name: RootExtension.root_pow
api.statement: The image of T^(1/p^n) has p^n-th power g.

api.name: RootExtension.star_comparison
api.statement: Record the almost isomorphism to the normalized integral model.

uses.how: Divisibility of T−g by every t^l and separatedness make T=g. Footnote 6 is essential: integral perfectoidness may initially hold only almost.

items.name: Almost faithful flatness of each neighborhood
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and each l>0, A/t→B_l/t is almost faithfully flat with respect to m_t.

items.name: Almost faithful flatness after adjoining roots
items.statement: For the extension A→A∞ of 2.2, A/t→A∞/t is almost faithfully flat with respect to m_t.

items.name: Derived completion and Koszul models
items.statement: Import derived completion for a finitely generated ideal, its Koszul model and the bounded-torsion or regularity hypotheses identifying it with a derived inverse limit of ordinary quotients.

api.name: DerivedCompletion.adjunction
api.statement: Export the completion reflector and its adjunction.

api.name: DerivedCompletion.koszul
api.statement: Compare with the inverse limit of derived Koszul quotients.

api.name: DerivedCompletion.reduce
api.statement: Reduction and completed filtered colimits commute only under the verified hypotheses.

uses.how: Do not replace derived quotients by ordinary quotients over arbitrary non-Noetherian rings.

items.name: Perfection of a simplicial F_p-algebra is discrete
items.statement: For a simplicial commutative F_p-algebra C, its filtered colimit along Frobenius is discrete and identifies with the perfection of π_0(C).

items.name: Root annihilation of torsion in a perfect ring
items.statement: If R is a perfect F_p-algebra with compatible roots of t and tx=0, then t^(1/p^n)x=0 for every n.

items.name: Almost discreteness of the derived root presentation
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and f_1,…,f_n,g in its integral tilt, let B be the filtered colimit over r of the Koszul complexes over A[T_i^(1/p∞)] on the relations (g^(1/p^r))♯ T_i^(1/p^r)−(f_i^(1/p^r))♯. Then Kos(B;t) is almost discrete. For an admissible rational presentation, derived t-completion of B is almost its integral rational localization.

items.name: Functorial almost faithful absolutely integrally closed extension
items.statement: For every integral perfectoid K°-algebra A there is a functorial extension A→B(A), almost faithfully flat modulo t, with every monic polynomial over B(A) admitting a root.
items.note: Existing node PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/andre-flatness-lemma read. Its statement does not explicitly give the functorial choice required here.

items.name: Almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: For a tower of A-modules M_n, almost-pro-zero means: for every k≥0 and n≥1 there exists m≥n such that t^(1/p^k) kills the image M_m→M_n. The later index may depend on both k and n.

api.name: AlmostProZero.iff_torsion_proIso
api.statement: For each k the inclusion of the t^(1/p^k)-torsion tower is a pro-isomorphism.

api.name: AlmostProZero.cofinal
api.statement: A cofinal reindexing preserves this condition.

api.name: AlmostProZero.eventual_transition
api.statement: Export the later index with its annihilation witness.

uses.how: This quantifier order is the input to all inverse-limit arguments.

items.name: Almost-pro-isomorphism of bounded derived towers
items.statement: A map of pro-objects in D^b(A) is an almost-pro-isomorphism if each cohomology tower of a cone is almost-pro-zero, with m_t fixed.

api.name: AlmostProIso.cone
api.statement: Characterize by almost-pro-zero cohomology of the cone, independently of cone choice.

api.name: AlmostProIso.comp
api.statement: Prove closure under composition using the cone triangle and annihilator bookkeeping.

uses.how: Use functorial representatives/coherent towers for taking cones and Rlim; state the boundedness used for the cohomological argument.

items.name: Tower separating two almost notions
items.statement: For a nontrivial root-valued base such as K°, let M_n=A/(t^(1/p^n)) with transition 1↦t^(1/p^n−1/p^(n+1)). These maps are injective, the tower is almost-pro-zero, and its pro-object in almost modules is nonzero.

api.name: AlmostProExample.transition
api.statement: Define the transition multiplication and prove compatibility.

api.name: AlmostProExample.transition_injective
api.statement: Use regularity of roots to prove injectivity.

uses.how: For fixed k, M_m is killed by t^(1/p^k) once m≥k. For any fixed transition into M_n, a sufficiently small positive root fails to kill its image in the valuation-ring example.

items.name: Derived inverse limit of an almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: If M_n is almost-pro-zero, every cohomology group of Rlim_n M_n is almost zero.

items.name: Almost-pro-isomorphisms induce almost inverse-limit isomorphisms
items.statement: A morphism of coherent countable towers of A-module complexes whose cone cohomology towers are m_t-almost-pro-zero induces an almost isomorphism on derived inverse limits. This applies to the actual bounded-complex comparisons in 3.2–3.5; coherence is retained in D(Tower(Mod_A)) or an equivalent enhancement.

items.name: A-linear functors preserve almost-pro-zero
items.statement: If F:Mod_A→Mod_A is A-linear and M_n is almost-pro-zero, then F(M_n) is almost-pro-zero.

items.name: Rational annular tower
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and g with compatible roots, put A_n=O^+({|t|^n≤|g|}⊂Spa(A[1/t],A)). The transition is A_(n+c)→A_n. Theorem 4.2 first assumes g is an almost nonzerodivisor modulo each t^m.

api.name: PerfectoidAnnulus.transition
api.statement: Restriction maps compose.

api.name: PerfectoidAnnulus.root_transition
api.statement: The root u_(n+c)^e of t^(n+c)/g maps to t^(ce)u_n^e.

api.name: PerfectoidAnnulus.base_map
api.statement: The maps A→A_n commute with transitions.

uses.how: The restriction direction and almost base must survive the quotient by t^m.

items.name: Pointwise almost-zero kernels
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, for every m≥0 and n≥1, ker(A/t^m→A_n/t^m) is m_t-almost zero.

items.name: Uniform root annihilation of cokernel transitions
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, working in m_t-almost modules, for every m,k≥0 the transition coker(f_(n+c))→coker(f_n) is annihilated by g^(1/p^k) for all n, where c=p^k m.

items.name: Quantitative Riemann extension
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, {A/t^m}_n→{A_n/t^m}_n is an almost-pro-isomorphism for the ideal generated by compatible roots of tg.

items.name: Uniform derived tensor version
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1 and fixed m≥1, for every k≥0 set c=p^k m. For every K∈D(A/t^m), every i and every n≥1, g^(1/p^k) kills the c-step transition on the kernels and cokernels of H^i(K)→H^i(K⊗^L_(A/t^m) A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m) in m_t-almost modules. Consequently (tg)^(1/p^k) kills those ordinary transitions, with c independent of n, K and i. For m=0 both rings modulo t^0 are zero.
items.note: The prior G4 chain-level gap is resolved at the paper-proof level by the amplitude-zero cone argument. This is not a claim that the derived tensor API is implemented.

items.name: Uniform estimates for Koszul homology
items.statement: For a regular sequence in A/t^m in the setup of 4.2, nonzero-degree Koszul homology of its base change to A_n/t^m forms uniformly almost-pro-zero towers. The underlying comparison applies to any finite Koszul complex, but vanishing of the source homology uses regularity.

items.name: Riemann extension without regularity of g
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and g with compatible roots, the final almost-pro-isomorphism of 4.2 holds without the almost nonzerodivisor hypothesis on g modulo t^m.

items.name: Riemann extension after limits
items.statement: Under the introductory setup, A∞→lim_n A∞⟨p^n/g⟩ is almost an isomorphism with respect to roots of pg, using the reductions and limits over m of 1.6.

items.name: Lifting flatness from one complete reduction
items.statement: For A Noetherian and A→B, if π is a nonzerodivisor on both rings, both are π-adically complete and A/π→B/π is flat, then A→B is flat.

items.name: Lifting faithful flatness from one complete reduction
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses as 5.1, faithful flatness of A/π→B/π implies faithful flatness of A→B.

items.name: Unramified regular local perfectoid cover
items.statement: For an unramified p-torsionfree Noetherian regular local A0 of residue characteristic p, there is a faithfully flat map to a field-based integral perfectoid algebra over the completed Q_p(p^(1/p∞)).

api.name: RegularPerfectoidCover.map
api.statement: Export the A0-algebra structure.

api.name: RegularPerfectoidCover.flat
api.statement: Export ordinary faithful flatness in the unramified case.

uses.how: Pass faithfully flatly to a complete ring with algebraically closed residue field; use Cohen presentation W(k)[[x_2,…,x_d]], adjoin compatible roots of parameters and p, and complete.

items.name: Ramified general perfectoid cover
items.statement: For p-torsionfree Noetherian regular local A0 of residue characteristic p, the construction in 5.2 gives a faithfully flat general integral perfectoid cover A′ before imposing a field-based root-of-p structure.

api.name: RamifiedPerfectoidCover.parameter_roots
api.statement: Export compatible roots of the Cohen parameters.

api.name: RamifiedPerfectoidCover.p_relation
api.statement: Export π^p=pv with v a unit.

api.name: RamifiedPerfectoidCover.faithful
api.statement: Export faithful flatness before star-normalization.

uses.how: After coefficient extension write A0=W(k)[[x_1,…,x_d]]/(p−f), f∈(x)^2 and p∤f.

items.name: Field-based normalization of the ramified cover
items.statement: Adjoin compatible p-power roots of the unit v to A′[1/p], take the completed integral closure A, and normalize by the almost-elements convention. The newly constructed A carries the K°-structure from compatible roots of p.

api.name: RamifiedFieldCover.root_p
api.statement: Construct roots of p from roots of π and v with the required compatibility.

api.name: RamifiedFieldCover.almostComparison
api.statement: Record the almost isomorphism involved in star-normalization.

uses.how: Almost purity supplies the almost faithful map. The root-containing ring at this point is A, not the original A′.

items.name: Almost Tor vanishing for regular local covers
items.statement: For p-torsionfree Noetherian regular local A0 with residue characteristic p, there exists field-based integral perfectoid A as in 5.2 with Tor_i^A0(M,A) m_p-almost zero for every A0-module M and i>0.

items.name: Ordinary-module detection by an almost cover
items.statement: For the same A0→A in 5.2, if M⊗_A0 A is m_p-almost zero then the ordinary A0-module M is zero.

items.name: Adic Hom comparison as a pro-isomorphism
items.statement: For Noetherian R, ideal I and finite R-modules M,N, {Hom_R(M,N)/I^n Hom_R(M,N)}→{Hom_R(M,N/I^n N)} is a pro-isomorphism.

items.name: Vanishing lim-one for the adic Hom tower
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 5.3, lim¹_n Hom_R(M,N/I^n N)=0.

items.name: Splitting obstruction
items.statement: For a map A→C in D(A), form its cone Q and the connecting morphism α:Q→A[1]. The unit splits if and only if α=0. For a finite injective ring extension C=B in degree zero, Q is B/A.

api.name: SplittingObstruction.zero_iff
api.statement: Give the equivalence between vanishing and a left inverse in the distinguished triangle.

api.name: SplittingObstruction.baseChange
api.statement: Derived base change transports the triangle and α coherently.

api.name: SplittingObstruction.annihilator
api.statement: The A-module Hom(Q,A[1]) supplies the annihilator ideal of α.

uses.how: The proof works with this morphism itself and its annihilator, not only a cohomology class of H^0(C).

items.name: Reduction to complete mixed-characteristic regular local rings
items.statement: To prove the finite splitting theorem, use localization, faithful flat completion and residue-field extension to reduce the mixed-characteristic branch to a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field and a finite domain extension generically étale after some nonzero pg.

items.name: Detecting a surviving finite splitting obstruction
items.statement: In the complete local finite-extension setup of 5.4, a nonzero splitting obstruction remains nonzero modulo p^m for some m≥3, and after the two almost faithful extensions there is k such that (pg)^(1/p^k) does not annihilate the resulting obstruction.

items.name: Almost purity for finite étale perfectoid extensions
items.statement: For a perfectoid K-algebra R and finite étale R-algebra S, S is perfectoid and S° is almost finite étale and uniformly almost finitely generated over R°. Faithfulness is a separate hypothesis when a cover or almost retraction is needed.

items.name: Almost splitting of a finite generically étale cover
items.statement: For the finite injective extensions over the rational perfectoid algebras in 5.4, finite étale after inverting p, the unit is almost split with respect to m_p.

items.name: Annihilation of the finite obstruction on each annulus
items.statement: For fixed m,n in the setup of 5.4, the obstruction after base change to A∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m is m_p-almost zero.

items.name: Recovering almost vanishing over A∞
items.statement: In the setup of 5.4, annular almost vanishing implies that the obstruction over A∞/p^m is m_(pg)-almost zero.

items.name: Direct summand theorem
items.statement: For a finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular, there exists an A0-linear map B0→A0 whose composite with the unit is the identity.

items.name: Perfect proper coherent cohomology over a regular local base
items.statement: For proper X→Spec(A0) with A0 Noetherian regular local, RΓ(X,O_X) is bounded with finite cohomology, hence perfect over A0. For any A0-algebra D there is a unit-compatible map from its derived scalar extension to cohomology of the ordinary base change. This map is not asserted to be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses.
items.note: Proper coherent finiteness and perfectness remain G5/G6. The comparison map to ordinary base-change cohomology suffices for 6.1; no isomorphism is needed there.

items.name: Generic multisection reduction
items.statement: Over a characteristic-zero fraction field, a proper surjective scheme has a closed point with finite separable residue extension. Its closure gives a proper dominating scheme which becomes finite étale after inverting a suitable nonzero pg.

items.name: Integral global functions in the perfectoid proper case
items.statement: For proper surjective Y→Spec(A) in the corrected 6.2 setup, B=H^0(Y,O_Y) is an integral A-algebra; B[1/p] is the finite étale generic algebra, and Y maps naturally to Spec(B).
items.note: Reclassified from missing after reading declarations at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Proper.lean:138 proves integrality for every universally closed morphism with affine target; no Noetherian or surjectivity hypothesis. QuasiSeparated.lean:401 identifies sections on a global basic open with localization for qcqs opens. GammaSpecAdjunction.lean:434,458 supplies the natural affinization map. The given proper morphism is qcqs, and Y[1/p] is its basic open for the image of p. Thus B[1/p]=Γ(Y[1/p],O), finite étale by the stated hypothesis. This is a composition of existing results, not a new general theorem to re-plan. No finiteness of B over A is asserted.

items.name: Admissible blowup domination of a generic isomorphism
items.statement: Let A be p-torsionfree and p-adically complete, and X→Spec(A) proper and an isomorphism after inverting p. There is a finitely generated ideal I⊂A containing p^N for some N≥1 and a factorization Bl_I(Spec(A))→X→Spec(A). Completing this diagram p-adically gives the formal domination required in 6.2. The algebraic factorization already suffices for the integral generic-fibre map.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.2; exact algebraic supplier Stacks 081T, rather than a domination theorem attributed to GR2 §15.4
items.note: The proof source for domination has been identified. Foundational flattening leaves are still G6; GR2 §15.4 is used for rational charts and integral stalks, not mis-cited as a standalone domination theorem.

items.name: Integral generic-fiber factorization
items.statement: For mixed-characteristic perfectoid K and normalized integral perfectoid K°-algebra A, let Sη=Spa(A[1/p],A). For every finitely generated I=(f_0,…,f_r) containing p^N, the integral locally ringed space (Sη,O^+) maps over Spec(A) to Bl_I(Spec(A)). Combining this with formal-domination gives a map to any proper model whose generic fibre is the identity.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.2 footnote 8; GR2 Release 6.95, Lemma 15.4.14(i)–(ii) and Remark 15.4.25(i)–(vi), pp. 1318–1324

api.name: IntegralGenericFiber.factor
api.statement: Construct the factorization through an admissible blowup.

api.name: IntegralGenericFiber.cohomology_map
api.statement: Export A→RΓ(Y,O_Y)→RΓ(Sη,O^+) and identify its composite with the unit.

api.name: IntegralGenericFiber.chartMap
api.statement: On U_i send the blowup ratio f_j/f_i to its bounded rational function; prove the full blowup-ring relations.

api.name: IntegralGenericFiber.overlap
api.statement: Identify the restrictions on U_i∩U_j via reciprocal bounded units.

api.name: IntegralGenericFiber.refinement
api.statement: For an actual morphism between dominating models, compare the corresponding maps using their chart restrictions.

uses.how: Take the induced maps on derived global sections, retaining the integral sheaf.

items.name: Integral almost acyclicity of a perfectoid affinoid
items.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid (R,R^+), O is a sheaf and H^i(Spa(R,R^+),O^+) is almost zero for i>0; in the normalized integral convention H^0 is the stated integral ring.

items.name: Almost derived splitting over a perfectoid base
items.statement: Let K be a mixed-characteristic perfectoid field, A an integral perfectoid K°-algebra, and f:Y→Spec(A) proper with f[1/p] finite étale and surjective. Then A→RΓ(Y,O_Y) has a left inverse in the almost derived category for m_p.

items.name: Derived direct summand theorem
items.statement: For any Noetherian regular ring A0 and proper surjective morphism f0:X0→Spec(A0), the unit A0→RΓ(X0,O_X0) admits a left inverse in D(A0).

items.name: Equal-characteristic splitting inputs
items.statement: For regular Noetherian Q-algebras, the finite direct-summand theorem follows from normalized trace and the derived statement from the characteristic-zero rational-singularity splitting result. For regular Noetherian F_p-algebras use the positive-characteristic direct/derived splinter results cited in the introduction.

items.name: Unbounded derived tensor from K-flat resolutions
items.statement: Import the E1 derived tensor bifunctor for module/sheaf-module complexes, constructed from K-flat replacements, with exactness in each variable, R-linearity, the unit isomorphism and its ordinary-derived-category comparison. Tensoring an arbitrary complex uses this derived functor, not its underived tensor on a chosen representative.
items.locator: EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1; Bhatt Remark 4.3; Stacks 06YF for the K-flat existence input

api.name: DerivedTensor.ofKFlat
api.statement: Use K-flat replacement and prove independence of that choice.

api.name: DerivedTensor.unit
api.statement: Identify R⊗^L_R K with K.

api.name: DerivedTensor.map_scalar
api.statement: Tensor a scalar multiple of a morphism as the same scalar multiple of the tensor map.

api.name: DerivedTensor.cone
api.statement: Compare tensor of a functorial cone with the cone of the tensor map.

uses.where: EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1; Bhatt Remark 4.3; Stacks 06YF for the K-flat existence input
uses.how: Uniform tensor annihilation uses R-linearity and exactness of this imported functor.

items.name: Cone of an almost injective module map
items.statement: For a commutative almost base (V,m) with m²=m and the standard flatness hypothesis on m⊗V m, a V-algebra R, and an R-module map u:M→N whose kernel is almost zero, Cone(u)^a is naturally isomorphic to coker(u)^a placed in degree zero. The isomorphism is natural in commutative squares of module maps.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3, expanded from Theorem 4.2(1); ordinary cochain convention H^(-1)(Cone(u))=ker(u)

items.name: Uniform tensor annihilation from module cokernels
items.statement: Let u_n:M→N_n be a compatible countable tower of module maps over R, each almost injective for m. Put Q_n=coker(u_n). If a·(Q_(n+c)→Q_n)=0 in almost R-modules for all n, then for every K∈D(R), a annihilates the transition Cone(K⊗^L u_(n+c))→Cone(K⊗^L u_n) in the almost derived category. The same c works for every K and every cohomological degree.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3; explicit derivation of its same-constant assertion

items.name: Uniform annihilation of tensor comparison defects
items.statement: Under uniform-tensor-cone, a kills the transition maps on both ker(H^i(K⊗^L u_n)) and coker(H^i(K⊗^L u_n)) in almost modules, for all i, with the same shift c. For m=m_t and a=g^(1/p^k), every t^(1/p^j)g^(1/p^k) kills the corresponding ordinary transition maps. In particular (tg)^(1/p^k) works with j=k.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3, long exact cohomology sequence of the tensor cone

items.name: Countable derived limit of coherent module towers
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and a strict countable tower of cochain R-module complexes K_n, define Rlim K as Cone(1−s:∏K_n→∏K_n)[−1], where s uses transition maps. This descends to D(Tower(Mod_R)), is exact, and computes the right derived inverse limit. The countable products are degreewise; these formulas are not asserted for arbitrary sheaf categories.
items.locator: Stacks 08TB, Definition 13.34.1 and Lemma 13.34.2; 07KV, Lemmas 15.88.1 and 15.88.9; Bhatt 3.4–3.5

api.name: TowerRlim.ofComplexes
api.statement: Form the product-difference cone with its degree shift.

api.name: TowerRlim.map
api.statement: A strict tower morphism induces its functorial cone morphism, preserving identities and composition.

api.name: TowerRlim.cone
api.statement: Identify the derived limit of a coherent cone tower with the cone of the induced limit map.

api.name: TowerRlim.cohomology
api.statement: Export the natural Milnor short exact sequence, retaining lim-one.

uses.where: Stacks 08TB, Definition 13.34.1 and Lemma 13.34.2; 07KV, Lemmas 15.88.1 and 15.88.9; Bhatt 3.4–3.5
uses.how: Use the resulting exact functor for the actual comparison towers in Lemmas 3.4–3.5.

items.name: Derived acyclicity of a pro-zero module tower
items.statement: For a countable pro-zero tower M_n of R-modules, 1−s on ∏M_n is invertible. Hence lim M_n=lim¹ M_n=0 and Rlim M_n=0. More generally, a levelwise morphism of module towers whose kernel and cokernel towers are pro-zero induces an isomorphism on derived inverse limits.
items.locator: Bhatt 3.4 proof input; Stacks 07KV, Lemmas 15.88.4 and 15.88.16; explicit product proof

items.name: Milnor sequence for coherent module-complex towers
items.statement: For the tower-roos construction and every integer i, there is a natural short exact sequence 0→lim¹ H^(i−1)(K_n)→H^i(Rlim K_n)→lim H^i(K_n)→0. If every H^i(K_n) is m_t-almost-pro-zero, then H^i(Rlim K_n) is m_t-almost zero.

items.name: Rees algebra and its degree-one generators
items.statement: For any commutative ring R and ideal I, reesAlgebra I is the subalgebra of R[T] consisting of polynomials whose degree-n coefficient lies in I^n. It is generated by the monomials aT with a∈I; if I is finitely generated, the Rees subalgebra is finitely generated over R without any Noetherian assumption.

api.name: reesAlgebra
api.statement: Use the existing subalgebra of polynomials.

api.name: reesAlgebra.monomial_mem
api.statement: The monomial aT^n belongs exactly when a∈I^n.

api.name: reesAlgebra.fg
api.statement: A finite generating set for I gives finite generation of the Rees subalgebra.

uses.how: Use this algebra in the affine construction of admissible-blowup; do not re-plan the Rees algebra.

items.name: Projective spectrum of a graded ring
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring and A_n additive subgroups giving an N-grading: A is their direct sum, 1∈A_0, and A_i A_j⊆A_(i+j). Then AlgebraicGeometry.Proj is a scheme. For a homogeneous element f∈A_m with m>0, its basic open as a locally ringed space is isomorphic to Spec of the degree-zero homogeneous localization at f.

api.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Proj
api.statement: Use the existing scheme associated to a graded ring.

api.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projIsoSpec
api.statement: Identify a positive-degree homogeneous basic open with its affine chart.

api.name: Blowup.reesGrading
api.statement: Supply the Rees grading and identify its degree-zero localized rings with blowup algebras; this adapter is not claimed as a pinned declaration.

uses.how: Applying this to the Rees grading and gluing relative Proj over the base remain adapters, not a new affine Proj construction.

items.name: Algebraic blowups away from an open subset
items.statement: For a scheme S, a quasi-coherent ideal I of finite type, and an open U on which I=O, form Bl_I(S)=Proj_S(⊕_(n≥0) I^n). A U-admissible blowup is a morphism isomorphic to one of these; the centre is part of a witness, not uniquely determined by the morphism. Over Spec(A), its charts are Spec(A[I/f]) for a finite list of generators f, with A[I/f] the subalgebra of A[1/f] generated by the ratios a/f.

api.name: AdmissibleBlowup.ofIdeal
api.statement: Construct the blowup from I, finite generation and I|U=O.

api.name: AdmissibleBlowup.chart
api.statement: Identify each standard chart with the actual blowup algebra A[I/f].

api.name: AdmissibleBlowup.overOpen
api.statement: Export the isomorphism over U and its compatibility with the structural map.

api.name: AdmissibleBlowup.universal
api.statement: Factor a map whose pulled-back ideal is an invertible ideal sheaf through the blowup.

uses.how: The blowup is projective for finite type I and is the identity over U. This is the algebraic modification used before p-adic completion.

items.name: Strict transform with exceptional torsion removed
items.statement: For X→S, a blowup S′→S in I, and a quasi-coherent module F on X, its strict transform is the pullback to X×_S S′ modulo sections supported on the exceptional divisor. On the f-chart it is (F⊗_A A[I/f]) modulo f-power torsion. The strict transform X′ of X is the closed subscheme cut out by that torsion in its structure sheaf; it is also Bl_(I O_X)(X).

api.name: StrictTransform.module
api.statement: Quotient the pulled-back module by exceptional-divisor-power torsion.

api.name: StrictTransform.chart
api.statement: Identify the f-chart quotient and show that f is a nonzerodivisor on it.

api.name: StrictTransform.scheme
api.statement: Identify the transformed scheme with the blowup in the pulled-back ideal.

api.name: StrictTransform.offCentre
api.statement: Recover X and F over the complement of the centre.

uses.how: Apply this construction to O_X in the flattening argument, retaining properness of X′ over S′.

items.name: Flattening by an admissible blowup
items.statement: Let S be qcqs, U⊂S a quasi-compact open, X→S quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and F a finite type quasi-coherent O_X-module. If F|_(X_U) is of finite presentation and flat over U, some U-admissible blowup S′→S makes its strict transform finitely presented over X×_S S′ and flat over S′. No Noetherian assumption is made.
items.locator: Stacks 0815, Theorem 38.30.7, statement and proof read; auxiliary leaves listed in G6

items.name: Flattening a finite type scheme generically of finite presentation
items.statement: For qcqs S, quasi-compact open U, and a finite type quasi-separated X→S whose restriction to U is flat and locally of finite presentation, some U-admissible blowup makes the strict transform X′ flat and finitely presented over S′.

items.name: A flat generic isomorphism is an open immersion
items.statement: If f:X→S is separated, locally of finite type and flat, and U⊂S is retrocompact and schematically dense with f^(-1)(U)→U an isomorphism, then f is an open immersion.

items.name: A proper generic isomorphism is dominated by a blowup
items.statement: Let S be qcqs and U⊂S quasi-compact open. Every proper X→S which is an isomorphism over U admits a factorization S′→X→S with S′→S a U-admissible blowup. Neither S nor X is required Noetherian.

items.name: Unit-compatible derived cohomology base-change map
items.statement: For any ring map R→D and a qcqs R-scheme X, put X_D=X×_R Spec(D). There is a natural D-linear map β:RΓ(X,O_X)⊗^L_R D→RΓ(X_D,O_(X_D)), compatible with the units from D. No flatness or Tor-independence is required to construct β; neither isomorphism nor almost isomorphism is asserted.
items.locator: Stacks 08HY, Remark 20.28.3; Bhatt Theorem 6.1 final diagram chase

api.name: CohomologyBaseChange.map
api.statement: Construct β for every ring map, as the adjoint of pullback of the counit.

api.name: CohomologyBaseChange.unit
api.statement: Prove the commuting triangle with the structural unit from D.

api.name: CohomologyBaseChange.identity
api.statement: For D=R identify β with the identity comparison.

api.name: CohomologyBaseChange.composition
api.statement: Check compatibility for two successive scalar extensions.

uses.where: Stacks 08HY, Remark 20.28.3; Bhatt Theorem 6.1 final diagram chase
uses.how: The triangle identities give β∘unit_derived=unit_ordinary. This is the sole base-change relation needed in the splitting argument.

items.name: Transfer a retraction across a compatible comparison
items.statement: In any category, if u:A→M, v:M→N, and r:N→A satisfy r∘v∘u=id_A, then v followed by r is a retraction of u. In D(D), an almost retraction of D→RΓ(X_D,O) therefore composes with cohomology-base-change-map to split D→RΓ(X,O)⊗^L_R D almost. A further derived scalar extension preserves a supplied retraction.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.1 final sentence and 6.2 change of base; elementary composition in a category

items.name: What this paper contributes over Andre’s proof
items.statement: Theorem 1.1 was proven by Andre; the paper states its own two contributions. (1) Andre's flatness lemma from [An2, section 2.5], reproduced in cleaned-up form as Theorem 2.3, is the essential new ingredient in the solution of the direct summand conjecture: using it, the conjecture is reproved using only the quantitative Hebbarkeitssatz, a simple linear statement about a fixed and explicit system of modules over a perfectoid ring (Theorem 4.2 and its proof), whereas [An2] relies on the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma of [An1], a deep non-linear assertion describing an entire class of algebras over a perfectoid ring. (2) The same techniques establish the derived version, Theorem 1.2, which has geometric implications inaccessible from Theorem 1.1: it implies that passage to alterations of a regular affine scheme can often be lossless for coherent cohomological purposes, and even the special case where the map is birational is a slightly nontrivial assertion about blowups, related to the work of [CR], and completely orthogonal to Theorem 1.1.
items.note: This is the paper's own statement of which route through the material is the cheap one, and it should govern the design: the linear Hebbarkeitssatz replaces the non-linear perfectoid Abhyankar lemma. It also warns that the derived theorem is not a formal strengthening - its birational case is orthogonal to the classical statement - so a blueprint cannot treat Theorem 1.2 as a corollary of Theorem 1.1.

api.name: DirectSummand.proofRoute
api.statement: The classical theorem is deduced from the flatness lemma and the quantitative Hebbarkeitssatz, with no appeal to the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma.

items.name: What each theorem needs from the quantitative Hebbarkeitssatz
items.statement: Theorem 1.6 says that the limiting isomorphism from Remark 1.7, that A_infinity is almost the limit of the A_infinity<p^n/g>, holds for diagrammatic reasons, so it remains true after applying any A_infinity-linear functor - such as Ext^i(N,-) for an A_infinity-module N - to both sides and then taking limits. The case i = 0 recovers Scholze's theorem, the case i = 1 is what Theorem 1.1 needs, and Theorem 1.2 relies on the statement for all i >= 0. With that in hand, Theorem 1.1 is proved by passing from A_0 to A_infinity losslessly using Theorem 1.5, passing to A_infinity<p^n/g> to push all ramification into characteristic p, constructing an almost splitting there by almost purity, and taking the limit over n using Theorem 1.6; it is exactly this last step where the approach diverges from [An2], which uses the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma. Theorem 1.2 is proved analogously: when the map is finite etale after inverting p, base change to a faithfully flat integral perfectoid extension and apply almost purity together with Scholze's vanishing theorem; in general one reduces to the generically finite, generically finite etale case and deduces it from Theorems 1.5 and 1.6.
items.note: The i-indexing is the useful content for planning: a blueprint that only wants the classical direct summand theorem needs the pro-isomorphism statement for Ext^0 and Ext^1, while the derived theorem needs it for all i, which is why Lemma 3.6 on A-linear functors is stated in the generality it is.

api.name: Hebbarkeitssatz.extFunctor
api.statement: Applying Ext^i(N,-) to the pro-isomorphism and taking limits preserves it, for every i >= 0.

items.name: The generality of the flatness lemma, and its attribution
items.statement: Theorem 2.3 is proven in [An2] under a more restrictive setup but with a stronger conclusion; the author records that Scholze pointed out that the same proof goes through in the generality stated here.
items.note: An attribution and scope fact a blueprint must respect: the statement formalised here is Bhatt's generalisation of Andre's lemma, not Andre's lemma, and Andre's version carries a stronger conclusion under narrower hypotheses. A design job importing [An2, section 2.5] must say which of the two it is importing.

api.name: FlatnessLemma.scope
api.statement: The hypotheses used here are weaker than Andre's and the conclusion correspondingly weaker.

items.name: The rational presentations also hold in the derived sense
items.statement: One might worry that the presentations of [Sc1, Lemma 6.4] used in section 2 are valid only in the non-derived sense, and so do not interact well with reduction modulo t or with t-adic completion; one may ask whether the displayed presentation is also true when the relations are imposed in the derived sense, that is when one works with the corresponding Koszul complexes. The answer is yes. The author records this although it is not needed for the purposes of section 2, because such presentations matter later.
items.note: This is the bridge between the ordinary presentations of section 2 and the Koszul models used later; the extraction already has derived-completion and derived-rational, and this remark is what licenses passing between the two descriptions. Bhatt calls it psychological comfort, but for a formalisation it is the statement that has to be proved rather than assumed.

api.name: RationalPresentation.derived
api.statement: The Koszul presentation computes the same object as the ordinary presentation, compatibly with reduction modulo t and t-adic completion.

items.name: A p-adic Kunz question, and its answer in the literature
items.statement: The proof of Proposition 5.2 goes through for any Noetherian ring A_0 admitting a faithfully flat extension which is integral perfectoid. The author therefore asks whether that condition characterises regularity, that is whether there is a p-adic analogue of Kunz's theorem, which characterises regularity in characteristic p as the flatness of Frobenius, and records that a positive answer will appear in forthcoming work with Iyengar and Ma.
items.note: That forthcoming work has appeared: Bhatt, Iyengar and Ma, 'Regular rings and perfect(oid) algebras', Communications in Algebra 47 (2019), no. 6, 2367-2383, arXiv:1803.03229, proves that a p-adically complete Noetherian ring is regular exactly when it admits a faithfully flat map to a perfectoid ring, with a version where flatness is relaxed to almost flatness. So a design job should import the characterisation rather than plan around an open question, and the extraction's regular-local reductions can be stated in the 'admits a faithfully flat integral perfectoid extension' form, which is what the proofs of section 5 actually use.

api.name: RegularRingSplittings.perfectoidKunz
api.statement: For a p-adically complete Noetherian ring, regularity is equivalent to admitting a faithfully flat map to a perfectoid ring.
